# Tags Input

> A text input that turns what you type into removable tags, for values with no list to pick from, submitted one entry per tag.

`<slab-tags-input>` · Form · built on `<input> + <button>s`

Docs: https://slab-elements.dev/components/tags-input/

## Import

```js
import 'slab-elements/tags-input.js';
```

## Usage

```html
<slab-tags-input
  label="Keywords"
  name="keywords"
  value="concrete, rebar"
></slab-tags-input>
```

Enter adds what's typed as a tag, and so does typing `delimiter`, a comma unless you change it, so a pasted list becomes several tags at once. Tags are trimmed, and a tag that's already there isn't added twice. With `max`, no more are added once there are that many, and what didn't fit stays in the input. What's typed is added when focus leaves too, so it isn't lost on a submit.

Each tag is a button before the input that removes it, named "Remove" and the tag unless you set `removeLabel`. `values` lists the tags in the order they were added, and each is submitted as its own entry, the way a `<select multiple>` submits them. The `value` attribute is the starting tags separated by commas, as on an `<input type="email" multiple>`. To pick tags from a list instead, use [Combobox](combobox.md) with `multiple`, whose tags work the same way.

Style a field with no tags through `:state(empty)` and one with `max` tags through `:state(full)`.

With `readonly`, tags can't be added or removed but the field can still be focused, read and submitted, where `disabled` leaves it out of the form. The tags are text rather than buttons, and the host is `:state(readonly)`.

## Keyboard

| Key                             | What it does                                                                                    |
| ------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Enter                           | Adds what's typed as a tag, or submits the form when nothing is typed.                          |
| `delimiter`                     | Adds what's typed before it as a tag.                                                           |
| Escape                          | Clears what's typed.                                                                            |
| Backspace                       | In an empty input, removes the last tag.                                                        |
| Left                            | At the start of the input, moves to the last tag.                                               |
| Left, Right                     | On a tag, moves to the previous or next one. Right from the last goes back to the input.        |
| Backspace, Delete, Enter, Space | On a tag, removes it and moves to the one that takes its place, or the input when there's none. |
| Escape                          | On a tag, goes back to the input.                                                               |
| Tab, Shift+Tab                  | Moves out of the field. The tags aren't Tab stops.                                              |

## Elements

### `<slab-tags-input>`

Import `slab-elements/tags-input.js` to register it.

A text input that turns what's typed into tags, with no visual styles. It's for values with no list to pick from, such as keywords or email addresses. When there is a list, use Combobox with `multiple`, whose tags work the same way.

Enter adds what's typed as a tag, and so does typing `delimiter`, a comma unless it's changed, so "red, green, blue" pasted in is three tags. What's typed is trimmed, and text that's empty, or a tag already there, adds nothing. With `max`, no more are added once there are that many, and what didn't fit is left in the input. When focus leaves, what's typed is added too, so it isn't lost on a submit.

Each tag is a `<button>` before the input that removes it. Backspace in an empty input removes the last, and Left at the start of the input moves focus to the tags, where Left and Right move between them and Backspace, Delete, Enter and Space remove one. In a right-to-left page, Left and Right swap. They aren't Tab stops, so Tab still leaves in one press. Enter in an empty input submits the form, as it does in a native one.

`values` lists the tags in the order they were added, and each is submitted as its own entry, the way a `<select multiple>` submits them. The `value` attribute is the initial tags separated by commas, as on an `<input type="email" multiple>`, and the `value` property is the current ones, joined by commas. "input" and "change" are dispatched together when a tag is added or removed, rather than on every keystroke.

`readonly` shows the tags without letting the user change them: the input can't be typed in, and the tags are text rather than buttons. It's still focused, read and submitted, where `disabled` leaves it out of the form, and never invalid.

Style it through its parts and through `:state(disabled)`, `:state(empty)` when it has no tags, `:state(error)`, `:state(full)` when it has `max` tags, `:state(readonly)` and `:state(required)`.

#### Attributes

| Name               | Type      | Default | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| ------------------ | --------- | ------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `label` (required) | `string`  |         | Names it. It's the accessible name, and the visible label where there is one.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| `delimiter`        | `string`  | `','`   | Typed or pasted, adds what's before it as a tag. Only Enter does when it's empty.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `disabled`         | `boolean` | `false` | Disables it, as `disabled` does a native control: the user can't focus or use it, and a form control's value isn't submitted.                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| `hide-label`       | `boolean` | `false` | Hides the label visually and leaves it as the accessible name, for a design that shows the label some other way.                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| `max`              | `number`  |         | The most tags the user can add. A `values` set with more keeps them all.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| `name`             | `string`  | `''`    | The name its value is submitted under, as a native control's `name`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `placeholder`      | `string`  |         | Shown while it's empty, as a native input's `placeholder`. It's a hint, not a label.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `readonly`         | `boolean` | `false` | Shows the tags without letting the user add or remove any. It's still focusable and submitted, and never invalid, as a native read-only input isn't.                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `required`         | `boolean` | `false` | Makes it invalid while it has no value, as `required` does a native control.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| `value`            | `string`  | `''`    | The tags, separated by commas, each trimmed. Like a native input, the attribute is the default value and the property is the current one. Use `values` for tags with commas in them.                                                                                                                                       |
| `custom-validity`  | `string`  |         | Makes it invalid with this message, as `setCustomValidity()` does, and shows the message at once rather than once validity is reported, for an error the page already knows about, such as one from a server. Removing it, or setting it to an empty string, makes it valid again, unless something else makes it invalid. |

#### Properties

| Name                            | Type                       | Description                                                                                                                                                                                |
| ------------------------------- | -------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `removeLabel`                   | `(text: string) => string` | Names each tag's button, which shows only the tag, from the tag. "Remove" and the tag in English when unset.                                                                               |
| `removedLabel`                  | `(text: string) => string` | What screenreaders are told when a tag is removed, from the tag. The tag and "removed" in English when unset.                                                                              |
| `addedLabel`                    | `(text: string) => string` | What screenreaders are told when a tag is added, from the tag. The tag and "added" in English when unset.                                                                                  |
| `values`                        | `string[]`                 | Every tag, in the order they were added.                                                                                                                                                   |
| `defaultValue`                  | `string`                   | The value it starts with, and goes back to when its form resets. It's the `value` attribute, as a native input's `defaultValue` is, so setting it sets the attribute, and `value` with it. |
| `form` (read-only)              | `HTMLFormElement \| null`  | The form it belongs to, or `null`.                                                                                                                                                         |
| `labels` (read-only)            | `NodeList`                 | The `<label>` elements associated with it, as a native control's `labels`: each `<label for>` that names its `id`, and a `<label>` around it.                                              |
| `validationMessage` (read-only) | `string`                   | What's wrong, as the validity message says it: the message given to `setCustomValidity()` or `setValidity()`, or else the browser's own. Empty while it's valid.                           |
| `validity` (read-only)          | `ValidityState`            | Its `ValidityState`, as a native control's.                                                                                                                                                |
| `willValidate` (read-only)      | `boolean`                  | Whether its validity is checked when its form submits. It isn't while it's disabled or read-only.                                                                                          |

#### Methods

| Signature                                                         | Description                                                                                                                   |
| ----------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `checkValidity(): boolean`                                        | Whether its value is valid. Dispatches "invalid" when it isn't, as a native control's does.                                   |
| `focus(options?: FocusOptions): void`                             | Focuses it, or the part of it that takes focus.                                                                               |
| `reportValidity(): boolean`                                       | Whether its value is valid. When it isn't, dispatches "invalid" and shows the validity message, as a native control's does.   |
| `resetValidityFeedback(): void`                                   | Clears the validity feedback without changing `validity`.                                                                     |
| `setCustomValidity(message: string): void`                        | Makes it invalid with a message of your own, or valid again with an empty one, as a native control's does.                    |
| `setValidity(flags?: ValidityStateFlags, message?: string): void` | Sets its validity and message, as `ElementInternals.setValidity()` does, for checks of your own beyond `setCustomValidity()`. |

#### Events

| Name      | Type    | Description                                                                                                                                                                             |
| --------- | ------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `input`   | `Event` | As the user changes its value, as a native control's does. Setting it from code doesn't dispatch it.                                                                                    |
| `change`  | `Event` | When the user changes its value, as a native control's does. Setting it from code doesn't dispatch it.                                                                                  |
| `invalid` | `Event` | When a check finds its value invalid, as a native control's does. Cancel it to leave the validity message unshown, after a blur, a submit or `reportValidity()`, and focus where it is. |

#### Slots

| Name               | Type                | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| ------------------ | ------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `description`      | `Element \| string` | Text that describes it, such as a hint or what the validity message means. It's its accessible description.                                                                                                                                                 |
| `validity-message` | `Element \| string` | Shown in place of the validity message's text while it's invalid and the message shows, for wording of your own, a translation, or a link. It's part of its accessible description, and `validationMessage` stays the browser's or `setCustomValidity()`'s. |

#### CSS parts

| Name               | Description                                                    |
| ------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `description`      | Text about the input, and its validity message when it has one |
| `input`            | The input                                                      |
| `label`            | The label                                                      |
| `tag`              | A tag's button, which removes it                               |
| `tags`             | The tags                                                       |
| `validity-message` | The validity message, which says why the value is invalid      |

#### CSS states

| Name               | Description                                                                                                               |
| ------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `:state(disabled)` | While it's disabled.                                                                                                      |
| `:state(empty)`    | While it has no tags.                                                                                                     |
| `:state(error)`    | While it's invalid and its validity message shows, which is once its validity is reported, as when its form is submitted. |
| `:state(full)`     | While it has `max` tags.                                                                                                  |
| `:state(readonly)` | While it's read-only.                                                                                                     |
| `:state(required)` | While it's required, for styles such as an asterisk.                                                                      |
